title: Efficacy of Intensive Visual Simulation (IVS) Before Exoskeleton-assisted Step Training in Patients With Hemisensory Syndrome With Brain Injury of Vascular Etiology.
official: Experimental Pilot Study: Efficacy of Preparatory Treatment With Intensive Visual Simulation (IVS) Prior to Step Training With an Exoskeleton (EKSO) in Patients With Hemisensory Syndrome Resulting From Acquired Brain Injury of Vascular Etiology.
summary: Clinical trial involving a medical device, not intended for CE marking, randomized, blinded to evaluate the efficacy of preparatory treatment with Intensive Visual Simulation 4 (IVS) prior to exoskeleton-assisted (EKSO) step training in achieving independent ambulation in hemiparetic patients with impaired proprioceptive sensation. Patients will be randomized into two groups: one group in which patients will undergo IVS treatment before physiotherapy and robotic step training with an exoskeleton; and one group in which patients will undergo only physiotherapy and robotic step training with an exoskeleton.

interventions.name: Rehabilitation treatment with IVS before step training using an exoskeleton
Rehabilitation treatment with step training using an exoskeleton

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Male and female patients aged 18 to 80 years (both ends included).
* Diagnosis of hemiparesis/plegia with proprioceptive sensory deficit due to a cerebrovascular event within the last 6 months
* Orientation in the 3 domains (space, time, and person)
* Cooperation
* Clinical stability
* Trunk control while standing
* Signature of the Informed Consent Form for participation in the study and for the processing of personal data

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patients aged \< 18 years and \> 80 years
* Patients who are disoriented in at least one of the three domains (space, time, and person)
* Non-cooperative patients
* Patients with global aphasia
* Patients with severe ideomotor apraxia
* Patients with cognitive or mental disorders
* Patients not eligible for EKSO:
* Severe comorbid conditions: infections, circulatory, cardiac, or pulmonary diseases, pressure ulcers.
* Severe spasticity (level 4 on the modified Ashworth scale).
* Spinal instability or unhealed fractures of the limbs or pelvis.
* Heterotopic ossification.
* Psychiatric or cognitive conditions that may interfere with the proper use of the device.
* Pregnant women.
* Reduced tolerance for standing due to orthostatic hypotension.
* Range of motion (ROM) limitations that would prevent the patient from achieving a normal bilateral gait pattern or performing normal transitions from a seated to a standing position and vice versa: Bilateral hip flexion less than 110°, knee flexion contracture greater than 12°, or inability to achieve neutral dorsiflexion of 0° with knee flexion up to 12°.
* Leg length discrepancy greater than 1.27 cm for the upper leg and 1.9 cm for the lower leg.
* Unresolved deep vein thrombosis.
* Uncontrolled autonomic dysreflexia.
* Lower limb prostheses.
